tasks.short: Provide checked technical answers on wells, hydrology, geology and code requirements.

steps.what: Clarify questions, site circumstances and the assistance requested
Retrieve applicable code requirements, well records and hydrologic references
Record the enquiry, verified location and supporting references
Draft technical information addressing the documented enquiry

loop.purpose: Draft an answer grounded in selected references
loop.input: Verified question, site context and applicable reference excerpts
loop.output: Draft answer with references and explicit unresolved points
loop.check: Hydrologist checks jurisdiction, reference currency, technical applicability and unsupported advice
loop.stop: One revision; absent authority or unresolved site applicability returns to manual answering
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot combine varied well conditions and reference explanations

steps.what: Evaluate technical advice, code applicability and necessary qualifications
Check and provide the final answer to the contractor or public enquirer

tasks.design: Configure reference retrieval in {DATA_PLATFORM} and an enquiry template in {HELPDESK}. A bounded draft in {DOCS} uses the captured enquiry and selected references; the hydrologist evaluates the advice and checks the exact final answer before providing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Varied questions require repeated reference retrieval and explanatory drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: A source-grounded draft can organise supplied technical explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Site applicability, code interpretation and knowing when investigation is necessary.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist can qualify advice and recognise missing site facts.
tasks.altitude: Reduce answer preparation while preserving accountable technical assistance.

reach.learn: Link each answer to applicable evidence

evidence.claim: Scopus AI provides cited abstract summaries with a warning against sole reliance; this is reference support, not authority for site-specific advice.
Enquiry-grounded drafting may reduce preparation time; the benefit estimate is unmeasured.

assumptions: Includes clarification, record capture, reference lookup, answer writing, professional evaluation and actual communication.
Hydrologist produces verified site/location, question, reference version and applicable excerpts in s1-s3, with capture counted in s3. Missing jurisdiction or site facts require manual clarification.
Native reference filters and response templates first; no model independently selects governing law or grants permission.
Ordinary enquiry saves remain retained and ungated; s6 checks the final external answer.
unknowns: Reference currency and repeatability of incoming enquiries
research_questions: How often does a draft remain usable after checking site applicability?

already_counted.description: Capture the question and verified reference context

incremental.description: Maintain reference scope and inspect answer quality

approvals.approved_version: Exact answer, qualifications, cited requirements and intended enquirer; changed facts or advice require a fresh check before communication.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89, gross=11, upkeep=4, central net=7 E1. Low: unusual drilling conditions and poorly indexed local requirements force manual reconstruction, retaining 96 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: current references and comparable well questions permit partial draft reuse but site assessment remains, retaining 92 hours plus upkeep for 4 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review site and permit applications and write a reasoned recommendation for the responsible authority.

steps.what: Retrieve site plans, permit applications and applicable requirements
Record application versions, locations and evidence references in the review worksheet
Review hydrologic implications, evidence adequacy and site-specific requirements
Determine whether to recommend approval, denial, modification or investigation
Write the recommendation, reasons, conditions and evidence references
Check and send the final recommendation to the permitting colleague

tasks.design: Configure application views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and a reference-linked review and recommendation template in {DOCS}. Scientific review and the recommended disposition remain human; a separate {EMAIL} step delivers the checked recommendation to the permitting colleague.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document indexing and repetitive recommendation structure add handling around expert review.
tasks.enabler_now: Native application views and reusable evidence fields can reduce that handling.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting requirements and determining whether evidence supports a disposition.
tasks.human_edge: The hydrologist can explain why a site requires investigation or different conditions.
tasks.altitude: Improve evidence traceability around a human permit recommendation.

reach.learn: Keep source versions attached to review reasons

evidence.claim: The digest reports difficulty with the permit decision tree, supporting caution about automating site-specific interpretation.
Native document indexing and recommendation templates may reduce clerical handling; this labour estimate is unmeasured.

assumptions: The task ends at an internal recommendation, not issuance of the permit or an applicant notice.

Hydrologist produces application ID, version, location and evidence references in s2, findings in s3 and recommendation reasons in s4-s5, with all capture priced. Missing versions or unclear jurisdiction require manual resolution.
Native views and templates first; no automated legal interpretation or recommendation outcome.
No self-approval on ordinary writing or save; only the actual send checks its final content and recipient.
unknowns: Quality of application metadata and standard recommendation format
research_questions: Which recommendation fields can be reused without weakening site-specific reasoning?

already_counted.description: Index evidence and capture recommendation text

incremental.description: Maintain review template and application view

approvals.approved_version: Exact recommendation, conditions, evidence versions and permitting colleague recipient; edits invalidate the send check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90.25, gross=9.75, upkeep=3, central net=6.75 E1. Low: revised drawings and unusual site conditions make indexing and reasons bespoke, retaining 97 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: stable application metadata supports indexing and some recommendation structure while technical reasons stay manual, retaining 93 hours plus upkeep for 4 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate glaciers, ice, snow and permafrost using documented observations and scientific interpretation.

steps.what: Define questions and methods for investigating glaciers, ice, snow or permafrost
Retrieve historical observations, imagery and relevant scientific records
Investigate physical properties and activity through field observations and measurements
Record location, timing, conditions, measurements and observation provenance
Interpret origins, properties and activity with explicit uncertainty
Write the investigation findings, methods and limitations

tasks.design: Use native observation catalogue filters and structured field records in {DATA_PLATFORM}, with a findings template in {DOCS}. Field investigation, interpretation and scientific wording remain human; the configuration reduces repeated navigation and record formatting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Historical sources and field metadata are inconsistently organised.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable catalogue views and observation forms may reduce clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Field access, comparable measurements and explanation of cryospheric processes.
tasks.human_edge: The investigator can recognise when local conditions undermine a comparison.
tasks.altitude: Strengthen traceability around direct scientific investigation.

reach.learn: Keep field context with each measurement

evidence.claim: Structured observation records and catalogue filters can reduce repetitive handling; this is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: Includes the research design, historical lookup, field investigation, observation record and written findings.

Hydrologist produces location, time, measurement, units, method, condition and provenance in s4; all capture time is counted. Missing contextual data require manual reconstruction or explicit exclusion from comparison.
Native views, forms and document templates first; no automated physical interpretation or fieldwork saving.
Ordinary record saves remain in retained time without a separate approval stage.
unknowns: Comparability of historic and new observations
research_questions: Which contextual fields are currently reconstructed after field visits?

incremental.description: Maintain observation fields and findings template

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92, gross=8, upkeep=2, central net=6 E1. Low: historical records lack locations or measurement methods and each field note is bespoke, retaining 98 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: comparable survey metadata permits form reuse but interpretation and uncommon observations remain manual, retaining 94 hours plus upkeep for 4 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile hydrologic information into checked map drafts and prediction inputs.

steps.what: Retrieve hydrologic information, geographic layers and atmospheric model inputs
Capture source versions, coordinates, depth datums, units and valid times
outputs: checked source manifest and transformation specification

steps.what: Compile compatible hydrologic sources into the working map and prediction dataset
inputs: checked source manifest and transformation specification

steps.what: Evaluate coverage, uncertainty and suitability for charts and predictions
inputs: checked source manifest and transformation specification

steps.what: Prepare navigational charts and maps from the evaluated geographic dataset
Run the existing atmospheric prediction method and inspect its diagnostics
Check chart metadata, map accuracy and prediction limitations
Save the checked charts, maps and prediction package in the existing project

tasks.design: Configure explicit source transformations in {DATA_PLATFORM} and chart templates in {OTHER}, the existing GIS and prediction tools. Separate compilation and rendering produce drafts; the hydrologist evaluates fitness, runs the existing prediction method and checks outputs before an ordinary retained project save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layer assembly and repeat chart layout consume attention needed for scientific evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic transformations and native GIS layouts can reuse an explicit source manifest.
tasks.still_hard: Datum compatibility, navigational accuracy and scientific limits of atmospheric inference.
tasks.human_edge: A scientist can reject a technically rendered output that lacks adequate evidence.
tasks.altitude: Make preparation reproducible while preserving expert acceptance of charts and predictions.

reach.learn: Check spatial reference and valid-time compatibility

evidence.claim: Copernicus openEO supports rerunnable scripts over satellite datacubes, demonstrating deterministic geographic data processing rather than navigational certification.
The proposed compilation and map-preparation benefit is an unmeasured scenario, unrelated to forecast accuracy gains.

assumptions: Produces working chart and prediction packages, including records and saving; formal navigation publication is not claimed or automated.

Hydrologist produces source ID/version, coordinate reference, vertical datum, unit, timestamp and transformation choice in s2; capture is counted. Layout specification is selected during s2 and evaluated in s4. Missing metadata or invalid conversions stop s3/s5 for manual repair.
OTHER means existing GIS and atmospheric prediction applications; native transforms and layouts precede custom pipelines.
Existing forecast computation and its human launch remain retained in s6; no saving or accuracy gain is attributed to it.
Same-system save s8 is fully retained with no self-approval; no external send is implied.
unknowns: Source layer compatibility and existing layout automation
research_questions: How often can the same source manifest and layout be reused without manual datum reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Capture and verify the transformation manifest

incremental.description: Maintain transformations and test chart metadata after source changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=64, gross=36, upkeep=5, central net=31 E1. Low: incompatible vertical datums, missing valid times and chart metadata force most compilation and layout work back to manual, retaining 91 hours plus upkeep for 4 net. High: aligned layers permit repeat compilation, but detailed chart output metadata and uncommon symbols need extra work, retaining 75 hours plus upkeep for 20 net.

role.altitude: Protect technical judgement while making evidence handling and draft outputs easier to reproduce.
reach: Work with permitting colleagues and geographic data specialists on traceable evidence
role.ambitious_version: A hydrologist who can explain and defend technical conclusions with less repetitive record and output preparation.
